D001-D008_h001.question:
For most of my adult life I’ve been pretty steady—organized enough to handle lesson plans, grading, coaching debate, that kind of thing. But about six months ago I started having these “up” periods that my wife says are totally unlike me. When those hit, that’s when everything goes off the rails.

During these spells I sleep maybe three or four hours and still feel wired, like I’m running on some invisible motor. At school I can’t sit still in the classroom; I’m pacing, popping into other rooms, starting a dozen projects at once. My desk turns into a disaster—half-finished unit plans, random Post-its everywhere—and I just can’t seem to put things in order even though I’m working nonstop.

My mind races. I jump from grading to redesigning the whole curriculum to thinking about starting a podcast. In the middle of teaching, I’ll lose the thread because some random idea pops into my head and pulls me away. I catch myself talking nonstop in class and at home, interrupting students and my wife, going on long tangents.  

When these “high” phases pass, I go back to my usual, more organized self. The distractibility and constant energy don’t stick around between those episodes.
D001-D008_h001.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

Between these high periods I’m much more like my usual self: I can focus, sit through meetings, follow directions, and I’m not nearly as restless or intrusive. The inattention and this motor-like energy only seem to show up when I’m in those intense, elevated phases.
